problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.statement: Find maximum profit from buying on one day and selling on a future day.
problems.intuition: Track the minimum price seen so far while scanning rightward.
problems.approach:
1. Track min_price = infinity and max_profit = 0.
  2. For each price, update min_price = min(min_price, price).
  3. Update answer = max(answer, price - min_price).
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Maintain minimum left value while scanning once

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.statement: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
problems.understanding: All characters in window must be distinct.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Check every substring with a set to see if it has duplicates.

problems.intuition: Variable-size sliding window with a set. Expand right pointer, shrink left pointer when duplicate encountered.
problems.approach:
1. Maintain hash set seen and left = 0 pointer.
  2. For right in range len(s):
  3. While s[right] in seen, remove s[left] from set and increment left.
  4. Add s[right] to set, update answer = max(answer, right - left + 1).

problems.title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
problems.statement: Given a string s and integer k, choose any character and change it up to k times to get the longest substring containing identical letters.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Check all substrings, count character frequencies, check if replacements <= k.

problems.intuition: Maintain sliding window tracking frequency of most frequent character in current window. Shrink left pointer when invalid.
problems.approach:
1. Use frequency map count and track max_frequency.
  2. Expand right pointer and update count and max_frequency.
  3. While (right - left + 1) - max_frequency > k, decrement count of s[left] and advance left += 1.
  4. Update answer = max(answer, right - left + 1).
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Valid Window Condition: window_length - max_frequency <= k

problems.title: Permutation in String
problems.statement: Given two strings s1 and s2, return true if s2 contains a permutation of s1.
problems.understanding: Check if any window in s2 of size len(s1) has identical character frequencies to s1.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Generate all permutations of s1 and search for each in s2.

problems.intuition: Fixed-size sliding window of length len(s1) using character frequency array comparison.
problems.approach:
1. Build target 26-element array for s1.
  2. Slide window of size len(s1) over s2.
  3. Add incoming character, remove outgoing character when index >= len(s1).
  4. If window array equals target array, return True.
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Fixed-size Window + Character Frequency Array Comparison

problems.title: Minimum Window Substring
problems.statement: Given two strings s and t, return minimum window substring in s containing all characters of t.
problems.understanding: Find shortest substring of s covering all character counts required by t.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Try every substring, verify if character counts meet requirements of t.

problems.intuition: Expand right pointer until window is valid (tracking formed == required). Then shrink left pointer while valid to find minimum length.
problems.approach:
1. Build need frequency map for t, tracking required = len(need).
  2. Expand right pointer and update have map.
  3. Increment formed when have[char] == need[char].
  4. While formed == required: record best window, remove s[left], decrement formed if needed, and advance left += 1.
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Expand until valid → Shrink while valid

problems.title: Sliding Window Maximum
problems.statement: Given an array nums and sliding window size k, return maximum element in each moving window.
problems.understanding: Find max value for each contiguous slice of size k.

naive.title: Naive Solution — Brute Force
naive.html: Extract sub-array slice of size k and compute max(slice).

problems.intuition: Monotonic Decreasing Deque: store indices whose values are strictly decreasing. Front of deque always holds index of max element.
problems.approach:
1. Use deque storing indices.
  2. Before inserting right, pop indices from back whose values <= nums[right].
  3. Pop front index if it falls outside current window deque[0] < right - k + 1.
  4. Append nums[deque[0]] to result once right >= k - 1.
problems.takeaway: Pattern — Max/Min over moving window → Monotonic Deque
